title: URL shortener
summary: Design a service that turns long URLs into short links and redirects visitors to the original URL.
functional: Create a short link for a long URL
Redirect a short link to its long URL
nonFunctional: Redirect latency under 50 ms at p99
Short codes must not be guessable in sequence
discussionTopics: Code generation: base62 of a unique ID vs random codes with collision checks
Data model: code -> long URL, owner, created_at, expires_at
Read path: cache hot codes (cache-aside), CDN or edge caching of 301/302
301 vs 302 trade-off (cacheability vs analytics accuracy)
Scaling writes: ID ranges per instance, or a sequence with batching
Abuse: rate limiting creation, malicious URL scanning
Analytics: asynchronous click events via a queue instead of a synchronous DB write
followUps: How do you guarantee custom aliases are unique under concurrency?
How would you count clicks without slowing redirects?
What happens when the cache cluster fails?

title: Distributed rate limiter
summary: Design a rate limiter that protects an API used by many clients across multiple API gateway instances.
functional: Limit requests per API key per time window
nonFunctional: Accurate enough across many gateway instances
Fails safely when the limiter store is unavailable
discussionTopics: Algorithms: token bucket, fixed window, sliding log, sliding window counter
Where state lives: local memory vs a shared store such as Redis with atomic scripts
Race conditions: atomic increment-and-check
Fail-open vs fail-closed when the store is down
Hot keys and sharding the limiter state
Communicating limits through response headers
followUps: How do you handle a sudden burst at a window boundary?
How would you limit by user and by IP at the same time?
How do you change limits without a redeploy?

title: Real-time chat
summary: Design one-to-one and small-group chat with online presence and message history.
functional: Send and receive messages in real time
nonFunctional: Messages are never lost once acknowledged
Low latency delivery for online users
discussionTopics: Connection layer: WebSockets, connection gateways, sticky routing
Routing messages between gateway nodes (pub/sub keyed by user or conversation)
Storage: partition by conversation_id, time-ordered message IDs
Ordering: per-conversation sequence numbers
Offline delivery: persist first, then push; push notifications
Presence: heartbeats with TTL, fan-out cost
Idempotent sends with client message IDs
followUps: How do you deliver messages to a user connected on two devices?
How do you handle a gateway node crash?

title: Notification service
summary: Design a service other teams call to send email, SMS and push notifications.
discussionTopics: API accepts requests and enqueues them; channel workers consume
Idempotency keys to prevent duplicates
Retries with backoff, dead-letter queues
Provider failover and circuit breakers
Rate limits per user and per provider
Preference and quiet-hours checks before sending
Tracking delivery status via provider webhooks
followUps: How do you prioritise a password-reset email over a marketing campaign?
How do you make sure an unsubscribed user gets nothing?
How would you test this end to end?

title: Payment processing
summary: Design the backend that charges customers through an external payment provider for an online store.
functional: Create a payment for an order
Handle provider success and failure callbacks
discussionTopics: Idempotency keys for create-payment
A payment state machine (CREATED -> PENDING -> SUCCEEDED/FAILED -> REFUNDED)
Unknown outcomes after timeouts: query the provider, reconciliation jobs
Double-entry ledger, immutable entries
Webhook verification and idempotent handling
Outbox pattern for emitting payment events
PCI scope reduction via provider tokenisation
followUps: The provider call timed out. Did the customer get charged, and what do you do?
How do you reconcile your records with the provider daily?
How would you support partial refunds?

title: Distributed job scheduler
summary: Design a system that runs scheduled and recurring jobs (like cron) reliably across a cluster.
nonFunctional: A job runs once per schedule even with many scheduler nodes
Handles thousands of jobs per minute
discussionTopics: Storing schedules with next_run_at, indexed for polling
Claiming jobs safely: SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED or leases
Exactly-once execution is impractical, so aim for at-least-once with idempotent jobs
Lease expiry and fencing tokens for long-running jobs
Retry policy and dead letters
Time zones and DST for recurring schedules
Separating the scheduler from the workers through a queue
followUps: A worker crashes mid-job. What happens?
How do you handle a job scheduled at 02:30 on a DST change day?
How do you prevent one tenant from starving others?
